discoveries.disposition: Same-record regional names; explicit links distinguish registered counterparts.
Do not invent a separate figure; longer Chinese form needs its own verified passage.
Existing record resolved; primary label correction and Burmese cult claims need Temple/Spiro passages.
Regional records retained; Heissig does not by itself support every Kalmyk/Buryat family claim.
Heissig p98 describes Geser consort; corpus conflation between White Brahma and Mongol Geser must be resolved before attaching spouse.

SN11.1 and SN11.22 read through SuttaCentral’s official text repository after website/alternate URLs failed. Suvira is a godling commanded by Sakka; biological fatherhood is not established by this translation. The anger-eating spirit is a narrative adversary, not a family member. Retained as narrative discoveries; no invented parentage or native personal-name assertion.
Primary Jataka535 opening read; five human forebears and two deva endpoints added. Fatherhood stays on human records; rebirth links connect heavenly bearers.
Dictionary distinguishes this namesake from Sakka daughter; not merged.
Qualified exact records added from the reviewed Wilson genealogy; no unsupported name equivalence.
Saci father lead; SB6.18.7 names Paulomi but is insufficient by itself to establish exact father identity.
Qualified AV3.10 bearer, not automatically Brahma or Daksha; office and bearer unresolved outside this passage.
Kalash connected by legacy equation; Avestan cognate lead requires passage review; no new identity edge.
References only; Shiva owns record. Requested reciprocal to Aditi for VP1.15 account; not implemented on shared endpoint.
Existing Hwanin aliases need modern religious context, not established by medieval gloss.
Mahabharata Adi Parva CXXIII, Ganguli, m01124.htm confirms divine father Indra, mother Kunti and Pandu’s request. Social father not conflated with biological default parents.
Direct dictionary entries read; office/bearer and previous animal birth distinguished. No counterpart-family transfer.
Accessible follow-up passages implemented; heavenly rebirth and acknowledged fatherhood kept distinct from biological parentage.
Both endpoints incorporated from Shiva-authored handoff a8994af; biological defaults unchanged.

names: Unnamed human wife and children of Kosiya
discoveries.disposition: Human wife and children are attested, but their personal names are not. Wife retained as unresolved external reference. Narada is an arbitrating ascetic, not a genealogical intermediary; no identity with the Hindu namesake inferred.
Named ascetic arbitrating the contest; not a genealogical intermediary. No identity with the Hindu namesake inferred. Retained as a narrative-only discovery.
RV10.72.4–5 endpoints incorporated from PR147 and this lane. VP1.15 and MBh66 reciprocals incorporated from Shiva-authored a8994af. No default parentage cycle.

names: Martanda and Aditi’s seven other sons in RV10.72
discoveries.disposition: Verses8–9 read; no automatic equation of the unnamed seven with every member of the later twelve-Aditya list. Existing solar identities require separate review.
Padma genealogy implemented. Female Pulomā, daughter of Vaiśvānara, is a distinct discovery; not merged with male Puloman. Irish and Balinese namesakes remain independent.

Indra’s daughter and maternal branch implemented. No Śacī maternity inferred. Wife of Ṛṣabha is a separate namesake, not silently identified. Śukra’s Indra-family reciprocal spouse endpoint is authored under the recorded ownership decision.
Namesake distinguished and father linked. Jātaka identification with Uppalavaṇṇā concerns a previous birth, not parentage; wider biography remains a separate review.
Chinese names retained on Śakra. Consort name in the quoted commentary is recorded as an unresolved regional identification, without importing Hindu parentage.
Thagyamin name, regional identity and cult location supported by NIU. The sibling nat images are contextual figures, not Śakra’s family.

names: Unnamed sons and grandsons of Suyaśā
discoveries.disposition: Maruts collective and both origin accounts implemented; Rodasi is a hymn associate, not an inferred wife or mother. Unnamed descendants retain no invented IDs. Suyasa and Rudra reciprocal endpoints requested from their owner.
